title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Controllable Data Generation
claim: A three-part framework discovers causal circuits for utility metrics, steers generation with them, then schedules the resulting data by training stage.
layout: 3 panels: left discovery column, right top generation, right bottom scheduling; rounded titled boxes
description: A wide figure split into three rounded, titled containers. The left tall panel, 'Training Utility Aware Circuit Discovery', has three numbered steps. Step 1 scores samples with metrics (AUM, EL2N, GradAlign) shown as circles with low/high buckets. Step 2 shows three network-graph icons in blue, orange and green: learnability, challenge and alignment circuits. Step 3 shows three small validation mini-panels: faithfulness, causal intervention and data filtering. A large blue arrow leads right. The top-right panel, 'Circuit Steered Data Generation', flows left to right from a seed MCQA dataset to target data profiles, then circuit steering with a gauge and funnel, then generated candidate documents. The bottom-right panel, 'Stage Aware Mechanistic Scheduling', shows three dashed stages (Warm-up, Transition, Challenge) with blue, orange and green blocks that change size across stages. The color coding is consistent throughout.
caption: Overview of the proposed framework. We first discover and causally validate internal circuits tied to specific training-utility metrics (Section [ref]). We then leverage these circuits to steer the generation process, curating distinct data pools with targeted optimization profiles (Section [ref]). Finally, our SAMS framework dynamically schedules these utility-targeted datasets according to the model's evolving learning phases during downstream fine-tuning (Section [ref]).
abstract: While recent advances in data synthesis aim to curate high-quality datasets, most generation pipelines still rely on heuristic prompt-based control. This black-box paradigm provides limited insight into how individual samples interact with a model's underlying learning dynamics. To bridge this gap, we propose a circuit-grounded framework that connects training-dynamics-based data valuation with mechanistic interpretability (MI). Specifically, we conceptualize data quality along three complementary utility axes, learnability, challenge, and alignment. First, we uncover specialized model-internal circuits that causally govern these utility signals. Then, moving beyond heuristic prompting toward mechanistic control, we leverage these circuits as controllable interfaces, actively steering generation to produce utility-targeted data. Building on this capability, we introduce SAMS (Stage-Aware Mechanistic Scheduling), which schedules circuit-steered data according to the model's evolving optimization needs. Experiments on multiple-choice QA tasks demonstrate that our approach yields precisely controlled data with greater diversity than prompt-based baselines, consistently improving downstream performance and calibration. Ultimately, this work establishes a principled white-box paradigm for interpretable data generation, pioneering the use of MI not just as an analytical tool, but as a practical, controllable interface.
